sections.h2: Where Riverhead sits and why the hamlet matters
sections.html:
Riverhead is the easternmost large town of the North Fork, set where the Peconic River reaches the bay. Of its 201.3 square miles, just 67.4 are dry land; water takes up roughly two thirds.

Within the town sit the hamlets of Aquebogue, Baiting Hollow, Calverton, Jamesport, Northville, Wading River and the downtown hamlet of Riverhead itself, plus parts of Laurel and Manorville. The hamlet your address falls in sets the school, library and fire districts that show up on the tax bill. Population was 35,902 in 2020 and is estimated at 36,394 for July 2025.

sections.h2: Who sells here, and what homes cost
sections.html:
A typical Riverhead house is valued at $486,600, and owners occupy 79.8 percent of homes. Tenants pay $1,974 a month, and the household in the middle of the income range takes in $94,249.

  • 14,202 households averaging 2.48 people.
  • Owner cost per month: $2,944 with a mortgage, $1,364 without one.

Many owners are past 65 and few move, so a lot of houses have been held for decades. The sellers who want a fast, simple close tend to be heirs and owners downsizing. Because the area is long settled, paperwork behind the house can decide a sale: certificates of occupancy, addition permits and septic records. Pull them together before you answer any offer.

sections.h2: Flood, water and the disclosure form
sections.html:
So much of the town is shoreline that water questions come up often. The town has Long Island Sound to the north, the Peconic River and bays, and four beaches that stay open all year. Basements, roofs and sump pumps all get tested by weather.

Real Property Law section 462 prints the disclosure form, and its questions to a seller cover floodplains, flood insurance, past flood claims, water in the basement, fuel tanks and septic age. Hand it over late, after the buyer has signed, and the buyer gets a $500 credit against the price. Answer only from what you know, and attach whatever radon, septic or mold reports you hold.

sections.h2: Rental permit rules for a house with tenants
sections.html:
Town Code Chapter 263 requires an owner to get a rental permit before renting out a dwelling, and the permit does not pass to a new owner. The Code Enforcement Division at 4 West Second Street handles applications, and the town now runs them through an online portal.

  • A permit applies to the whole premises, and a multi-family house needs one for each rented unit.
  • Stays of 29 days or fewer count as transient rentals, which the code bans.
  • Whoever buys must register the property inside 30 days after title closes.
  • First offenses carry fines of $250 to $1,000, and each additional week can count as a separate violation.

The town's summary of Chapter 263 shows a $300 fee for a two-year permit. Call Code Enforcement for the current fee. If your tenant moves out before closing, a lapsed permit is one more item a buyer's attorney may raise, so ask the office what it would take to put the file in order.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and penalties
sections.html:
Riverhead's Receiver of Taxes mails one bill in mid-December and splits it into two halves, due about January 10 and May 31. A weekend due date slides to Monday, which is why recent halves landed on January 12 and June 1. The receiver collects town, county, school, fire and special district taxes together.

Riverhead late-payment penalties on the first half
Payment datePenalty
December 1 to January 12None
After January 121%
After February 102%
After March 103%
After April 104%
After May 115%

After June 1 the unpaid balance is owed to the Suffolk County Comptroller, and parcels still behind move to the county tax lien sale in November or December. The tax year runs December 1 to November 30. Report the sale to the receiver's office afterward, since a bill may carry the old owner's name for as long as six months. If the buyer cannot claim your exemptions, a pro-rata charge appears, and the closing attorney should prorate with that in mind.

sections.h2: Recording the deed with the Suffolk County Clerk
sections.html:
Deeds for Riverhead properties are recorded with the Suffolk County Clerk. The deed schedule lists a base cost of $245 plus $5 for each page, and the filing must include the state transfer tax form TP-584 and the real property transfer report.

State transfer tax is charged on any conveyance above $500, at two dollars for each $500 of the price, with part of a $500 block counted as a whole one. The mansion tax also applies to residential sales of $1,000,000 or more, paid by cash or certified check. For the tax map number, ask the Town Assessor. Most sellers leave this to the closing attorney, though recording happens separately from the signing.

sections.h2: Picking a sale route when time is short
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, run the sale yourself, or take an offer from a cash buyer. Let the repair list and your calendar decide.

  • A listing puts the house in front of the widest crowd, but showings, repair requests and a buyer's mortgage approval each add weeks.
  • Going it alone keeps the commission in your pocket, yet you price the house, fill in the disclosure form and handle the contract.
  • A cash offer fits a house with deferred repairs, rental permit trouble, an inherited title or a firm deadline. Get the number in writing and set it beside what a listing would leave you after fix-ups and closing charges.

Before any of the three, put the rental permit, current tax bill, disclosure statement and septic or oil tank records in one folder.

sections.h2: What happens between an accepted offer and closing
sections.html:
After the contract is signed, the buyer's attorney will usually ask for the latest tax bill, septic or oil tank records and, if the house was ever rented, the permit. Your attorney requests a payoff figure from the Receiver of Taxes, or from the county Comptroller once the bill has moved there.

You sign the deed and transfer forms at the table. Filing comes afterward as a separate step, when the county clerk takes the transfer tax and per-page charges. With cash there is no appraisal and no loan approval, so the schedule hangs on title, the permit file and how fast the receiver sends figures. Mention anything unusual, like an unpermitted unit or a flood claim, at the start.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Riverhead house if it was rented without a permit?
faqs.a: Yes, but expect questions. Chapter 263 makes renting without a permit a violation, and the permit is not transferable, so a buyer must register within 30 days of closing. Ask Code Enforcement what it would take to get the file in order before you list.

faqs.q: Who do I pay Riverhead property taxes to?
faqs.a: Until June 1, pay the Town of Riverhead Receiver of Taxes at 4 West Second Street. Later payments of an unpaid balance go to the county Comptroller, 330 Center Drive in Riverhead.

faqs.q: How do I find my Riverhead school district?
faqs.a: The hamlet decides. Four districts bill through the receiver here: Riverhead, Shoreham-Wading River, Mattituck-Cutchogue and Eastport South Manor, and the name is on your tax bill.

faqs.q: Does the seller or the buyer pay New York transfer tax?
faqs.a: The county clerk collects the tax with the deed, at two dollars per $500 on sales above $500. Your contract decides who pays, so have your attorney check that clause before you sign.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed after closing in Riverhead?
faqs.a: The Suffolk County Clerk records it and takes the fees and taxes in the same visit. Call (631) 852-2000 with questions.
